previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including systolic heart failure, stage IV chronic kidney disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, coronary artery disease, and chronic pain on opioids was admitted for bilateral leg swelling and pain. She presented with acute on chronic heart failure and acute kidney injury, likely due to fluid overload from excessive fluid intake and high salt consumption. Hyponatremia and encephalopathy were attributed to volume overload and medication accumulation, particularly gabapentin, which was held and later restarted at a reduced dose. Treatment with intravenous Lasix improved her volume status, renal function, and mental clarity. Her oxycodone dose was reduced, and she was discharged home on her baseline diuretic with instructions for daily weight monitoring and close follow-up. A left foot X-ray revealed soft tissue edema and a foreign body in the hallux, which was removed. She improved clinically and was discharged in stable condition.

Brief Hospital Course:
========
SUMMARY:
========
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with HFpEF, CKD, 
CAD s/p PCI, and DM2, who is re-admitted for her second HFpEF 
exacerbation in the last month, c/b severe Hypervolemic 
hyponatremia. These issues have resolved with IV diuresis. 

============
TRANSITIONS:
============

[ ] Discharge diuretic regimen was significantly increased from 
20mg torsemide daily to 60mg BID. Her discharge weight was 
69.95kg/154.2lbs and creatinine 3.5. Please adjust her diuretic 
dosage as needed 

[ ] noted to be mildly hyperphosphatemic with Phos of 5.3 on day 
of discharge. Consider need for phosphate binders 

[ ] Please uptitrate carvedilol as tolerated. Her home dose 
(50mg carvedilol BID) was reduced while inpatient due to 
decreased blood pressures 

[ ] Ms. ___ has baseline ___ ___ with profound macrocytosis. 
B12 and iron studies normal. We would recommend workup for MDS 
or other causes and possible referral to hematology-oncology for 
this. 

=============
ACUTE ISSUES:
=============
#Acute on Chronic HFpEF exacerbation
Patient was discharged 10d prior to admission for similar HFpEF 
exacerbation. Since then, due to dietary misunderstanding (was 
told to drink lots of water and was not aware of salt 
restriction) she gained 10lbs in the interim and presented due 
to leg swelling and weight gain. She was placed on furosemide 
drip however had significant rise in her creatinine, 
subsequently diuresed with furosemide 120IV PRN and transitioned 
to PO torsemide 60mg BID to maintain euvolemia. To maintain 
aggressive diuresis with appropriate blood pressures, her home 
carvedilol dose was decreased. 

Her discharge weight was 69.95kg/154.2lbs and creatinine 3.5.

#Hyponatremia
On presentation, sodium was 115 which necessitated ICU 
admission. Presumed to be hypervolemic hyponatremia. Renal was 
consulted per protocol. Her sodium was closely monitored and 
improved with furosemide diuresis as described above, with rate 
of rise no more than 6mEq/day. At discharge, sodium was 137 and 
she had been eunatremic for several days prior. 

# ___: 
# CKD IV-V
# Secondary hyperparathyroidism
On admission, her baseline serum creatinine was presumed to be 
2.8; She initially presented with ___ that was likely 
cardiorenal. During aggressive diuresis with furosemide drip, 
her creatinine peaked to 3.9, and so diuresis was slowed for 
this. Her discharge serum creatinine is 3.4-3.5 which we believe 
is her new baseline. Her home sodium bicarbonate and calcitriol 
supplements were continued. She does not currently take any 
phosphate binders and was not initiated on any at discharge. 

===============
CHRONIC ISSUES:
===============

#Macrocytic anemia
#Pancytopenia
She has had a longstanding history of macrocytic anemia of 
unclear etiology. Her baseline Hb is ___. B12 and iron studies 
within the last 2 months were normal. Additionally noted to be 
leukopenic on admission which resolved without intervention, as 
well as thrombocytopenic which we believe is from her history of 
cirrhosis. Other etiologies of macrocytic anemia include MDS 
given profound macrocytosis for which she should be evaluated by 
hematology-oncology. 

# Troponinemia, resolved
On admission. Plateaued at 0.03. No EKG changes. Most likely iso 
CKD,
potentially related to demand from CHF exacerbation. 

This patient was prescribed, or continued on, an opioid pain 
medication at the time of discharge (please see the attached 
medication list for details). As part of our safe opioid 
prescribing process, all patients are provided with an opioid 
risks and treatment resource education sheet and encouraged to 
discuss this therapy with their outpatient providers to 
determine if opioid pain medication is still indicated.
